extracted.intended_audience: Individuals with public information responsibilities (primary or auxiliary) at the state, local, tribal, or territorial level of government (Public Information Officers)
extracted.subtask_description: An instructor-led one-day training course that prepares public information officers to establish, operate, and lead a Joint Information System/Joint Information Center (JIS/JIC) in multi-agency incidents, applying NIMS multi-agency coordination principles and strategic communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and operate a JIS/JIC
rubrics_metrics.description: Equip PIOs with the skills needed to establish and operate a JIS/JIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course builds on solo PIO competencies from L0290 and applies those skills in an expanding incident where coordination is enhanced through activation of a Joint Information System (JIS) and establishment of a Joint Information Center (JIC). Training is instructor-led and uses discussion, lecture, and active participation in exercises to provide a realistic, scenario-driven approach to mastering these skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working knowledge of PIO operational practices within NIMS Multi-Agency Coordination System
rubrics_metrics.description: Impart a working knowledge of operational practices for performing PIO duties within the NIMS Multi-Agency Coordination System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should understand how PIO duties function inside multi-agency coordination structures and how operational practices scale and flex at the local level to interface with state and federal partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate messages in a multi-agency environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the importance of coordinating messages in a multi-agency environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes harmonizing communications among multiple agencies to ensure consistent, accurate public information during incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate JIS and JIC
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe and differentiate between the Joint Information System (JIS) and the Joint Information Center (JIC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants must be able to articulate roles, purposes, and relationships of the system-level JIS versus the physical/operational JIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply strategic communications process in a JIC
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the strategic communications process to managing information in a JIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers using strategic communications principles (e.g., audience analysis, messaging, coordination, channels) to manage information flow and public messaging within a JIC environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess management practices and capabilities for organizing a local JIC
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess current management practices and capabilities to organize and lead a local JIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should evaluate existing local structures, identify gaps, and determine readiness to stand up and lead a JIC effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify organizational structures and resources for coordination with state and federal JIC partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify organizational structures and resources to facilitate operations with state and Federal JIC partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on recognizing relevant partner roles, resource needs, and procedures for interoperable operations across jurisdictions and levels of government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize and lead a JIC in a scenario
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a scenario, organize and lead a JIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical demonstration expectation: participants will practice organizing and leading a JIC using scenario handouts and exercises to apply concepts in a realistic, time-compressed setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate mastery through scenario-driven exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Master the required skills through realistic, scenario-driven exercises that include active participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course delivery methods (discussion, lecture, active exercises) are intended to support demonstration of competencies; materials include a training manual, scenario handouts, and optional JIC job aid to guide performance and evaluation.
